### 18.51 A settlement by a mark, and a bound request, at a full scope

New in revision 21 (sections 6.4 and 17.2a; the planner's act
`1f8aba72`). M is a made-up value of platform data. Its item type `job`
has the states `open`, `busy` and `done`, of which `done` is final; a
fixed reference `owner`, a scope; a value slot `flagged` of the type
`bool`, required, with `default: false`; and `holds: { decisions: {
stop: 1 } }`. The handler `start` of a request opens a `job`. The
handler `flag` of a `tell` states `settles: { of: "also.job", sets:
"flagged", in: ["open", "busy"] }`, a guard, and one `value` effect that
sets `flagged` to `true`. The handler `stop` of a `tell` states `bound:
{ of: "also.job", where: [{ equals: { a: { sender: true }, b: { slot:
"owner", of: "also.job" } } }] }`, a guard `{ state: ["open"], reason:
"too-late" }`, and an effect that sets the state `done`. No handler
sends a request, and M has no timed rule. G is a scope under M with a
budget of entries. Every number is made up.

| Case | The input | Judged | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The data of M, with the platform option | The third form of `settles`, `decisions` and `bound`. | It validates. A `job` that is `open` or `busy` with `flagged` false reserves 1 entry for the mark, by row 3. A `job` that is not final reserves 1 entry for one `stop`. |
| 2 | The data of M, where `in` lists `done` | A final state. | It does not validate. |
| 3 | The data of M, where an act sets `flagged` from a field | A written effect sets the mark otherwise than to `true`. | It does not validate. |
| 4 | A `start` to G, whose free room is 3 entries | New work: its entry, 1 for the mark and 1 for the decision. | Written. With room for 2 it is not decided, and transport answers "retry". |
| 5 | A `flag` for that job, which is `busy`, at G with no free room | The job awaits the mark, and the entry sets it. | Settling. Written. `flagged` is `true`, and reserved falls by 1. |
| 6 | A second `flag`, as a new request, at G with no free room | The mark is `true`: the job awaits nothing. | New work. Not decided. Transport answers "retry". |
| 7 | A first `flag` whose guard fails | A refusal sets no mark. | New work. With no free room it is not decided. |
| 8 | A `stop` from the job's owner, when the job is `busy`, at G with no free room | Bound: the fields are typed, the job is not final, the sender is the owner and the count is 1. The guard fails. | Settling. Written, decided `refused`, `too-late`. The entry holds no effect. The count of `stop` is 0, and reserved falls by 1. |
| 9 | The same `stop`, when the job is `open` | Bound. The guard holds. | Settling. Written, decided `applied`. The job is `done`. |
| 10 | A `stop` from another scope than the owner, at G with no free room | The `where` fails. | Not bound: new work. Not decided. Transport answers "retry". |
| 11 | After case 8, a second `stop` from the owner, as a new request | The count is 0. | Not bound: new work. |
| 12 | A repeat of the request of case 8 | It was decided. | Answered from its deciding entry. Nothing is drawn, and nothing is written. |
| 13 | The job becomes `done` while `flagged` is false and its count of `stop` is 1 | It leaves the states of `in`, and it is final. | It awaits nothing and holds nothing. Both entries are released. |
| 14 | A replay of the entries of cases 5 and 8 | It derives that each is settling, the draw and both amounts. | `consistent`. With case 8 read as new work on a full scope: `mismatch`. |

Owner: B1 for cases 1 to 3; B2 for cases 4 to 13, on real storage; B9
for case 14. This shows that a notice which sets a mark, and the
decision of a rightful request whatever it is, are recordable with no
free room, and that a request which is not bound is not.

Read with revision 22: the name `job` of `flag` and of `stop` is read as
bound by a written rule, by a field of the type `item`. That source
stands. Witness 18.53 has a selector as the source. In case 1, the 1
entry for the mark is the marker duty (job, `flagged`). Witness 18.54
has an item with two marks.

### 18.52 Two steps of observations, rows that overlap, and the signer

New in revision 21 (section 16.1). M is a made-up value of platform
data. Its kind `weigh` of `outcomes` states `origin: "opening"` and
three rows. R1: `{ of: "rules", window: 10, use: "once", without: "wait"
}`. R2: `{ of: "key", from: "rule", max: 3, second: true, window: 10,
use: "once", without: "wait" }`. R3: `{ of: "key", from: "rule", max: 2,
window: 10, use: "once", without: "write" }`. Its act `set` has a field
`a` of the type `member`, and one row: `{ of: "member", from: { field:
"a" }, max: 1, window: 300, use: "reuse" }`. G is a scope under M. The
`uses` of an outcome's origin name two entries of a lane: the deciding
entry of a check c1, signed by the key k1, and of a check c2, signed by
k2. Every rule is a stand-in.

| Case | The input | Judged | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The data of M, with the platform option | Each row passes the ten checks. | It validates. |
| 2 | The data of M, where the row of `set` states `from: { signer: true }` | Check 10. | It does not validate. |
| 3 | The data of M, where the row of `set` reads a slot of a subject whose name of `also` a mark binds | Check 10. | It does not validate. |
| 4 | The data of M, where the row of `set` states `second` | Check 9. | It does not validate. |
| 5 | An outcome of `weigh`. The rules that G observes require c1 and not c2. The rule of R3 names k1 and k3. The rule of R2, given the observation of the rules, names k1. | The first step reads the rules, k1 and k3. The second step gives k1, which is at hand. | Written. `observed` holds three records: the rules, k1 and k3. k1 was read once. Each row is whole. |
| 6 | The same, when k3 cannot be read | R3 is absent, and states `write`. R2 gives k1 and is whole. | Written. `observed` holds the rules and k1. The rule is told that R3 is absent. |
| 7 | The same as case 5, when k1 cannot be read | R2 is absent, and states `wait`. | Not written. The outcome stays offered, and its operation keeps its reservation. |
| 8 | In the commit of case 5 the observation of the rules is past its window. It is read again, and now requires c2 too. | The second list holds k2, with no observation at hand. | The commit stops. k2 is read, and the turn starts again. |
| 9 | The same as case 5, when the rule of R3 names k1, k3 and k4 | R3 is over: 3 is more than its `max` of 2. | Written. `observed` holds the rules and k1, which R2 gives. The rule is told that R3 is over. |
| 10 | `set`, where `a` is the signer's own member, and the grant's observation is 40 seconds old and `reused` | The subject is the `member` of the grant's observation, inside 300 seconds, and the row states `reuse`. | Written. The grant serves the subject, and the input has no `observed`. |
| 11 | A replay of the entry of case 5 | It derives the first list, then the second from the recorded observation of the rules. | `consistent`. With a record of k2 added: `mismatch`. |
| 12 | A replay of the entry of case 6 | k3 has no record, so R3 is absent, and it states `write`. | `consistent`, with `observation-read` under `trusts`. |

Owner: B1 for cases 1 to 4; B2 for cases 5 to 10, on real storage with a
controlled clock; B9 for cases 11 and 12. The rules are stand-ins. This
shows the order of the reads and what an entry retains. It proves
nothing about a rule of a destination.

### 18.53 A bound request finds its item by a selector, at a full scope

New in revision 22 (section 17.2a, "The source of `bound.of`"; the
verdict `dc1da38a`, its first finding). Changed in revision 23 (section
17.2a, "An index that an item type declares"; the verdict `675776bc`;
the planner's act `2d3fa911`): the selector uses a declared index. The
setup states the index. Cases 1, 4, 9 to 11, 13, 15 and 16 are stated
again, and cases 18 to 25 are new. Two cases of revision 22 no longer
hold as they were written. Case 1 accepted a mark with `code`, `row` and
`item` only: that mark is now case 18, and is refused. Case 16 set a
runtime that reads every job beside one that keeps an index: no runtime
may read every job now.

M is a made-up value of platform data. Its item type `board` is not
`many`, and has two references to a `job`: `slot` and `judging`. Its
item type `job` is `many`. It has the states `queued`, `taken`, `gone`
and `done`, of which the last two are final; a fixed and required fact
`ticket`, of an entry of the sender's definition; a fixed and required
reference `owner`, a scope; `indexes: ["ticket"]`; and `holds: {
decisions: { stop: 1 } }`. The handler `start` of a request opens a
`job`, `queued`, with `ticket` from its field and `owner` from the
sender. It has no guard on an earlier job of the same ticket. The
handler `stop` of a `tell` has one field, `ticket`, which is required
and of the type of the slot, and `opens: null`. Its name `job` of `also`
is the mark `{ code: "job-of", row: "P15", item: "job", index: "ticket",
key: "ticket" }`. Its rule is given the jobs that the index returns for
the field's ticket. It gives the one of them that is not final, or the
last of them where each is final. The handler states `bound: { of:
"also.job", where: [{ equals: { a: { sender: true }, b: { slot: "owner",
of: "also.job" } } }] }`; a guard with the same two operands and the
reason `not-owner`; the guard `{ state: ["queued"], of: "also.job",
reason: "too-late" }`; an effect that sets the state `gone`; and an
effect mark `open-stopped` with `most: { effects: 2, opens: "job" }`,
whose rule opens a job and leaves it `gone` when the selector gives
none. M has no timed rule and no `settles`, so `dec(m)` for `stop` is 1
entry. G is a scope under M with a budget of entries and no free room.
It holds three jobs, each with a count of 1 for `stop`: A, of the lane
P, `queued`, which `board.judging` names; B, of the lane Q, `queued`,
which neither reference names; and C, of the lane R, `taken`, which
`board.slot` names. Each has its own ticket. Every rule is a stand-in,
and every number is made up.

| Case | The input | Judged | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The data of M, with the platform option | `job-of` binds the name that `bound.of` names. It stands at place 2, and its `item` lists `stop` in `decisions`. It states `index` and `key`, and no member beside the five. `job` lists `ticket` in `indexes`, and that slot is fixed, required and of the type `fact`. The field `ticket` of `stop` is required and of the same type. | It validates. `job-of` is a binding selector. |
| 2 | The data of M, where the mark `job-of` states `clock` | A mark with another member is the source. | Refused by the validator, `bound-source`. |
| 3 | The data of M, where `bound.of` names a name that is bound `via` a slot of a name which a mark binds | The source is reached through a mark. | Refused by the validator, `bound-source`. |
| 4 | A `stop` from Q with the ticket of B | The index returns B for that ticket, and no other job. The rule is given B and the field, and gives B. B is not final, the sender is its owner, and its count is 1: bound. The guards hold. | Settling. Written, decided `applied`. B is `gone`. The count of B is drawn. Used rises by 1 and reserved falls by 1. A and C are as they were. |
| 5 | The same `stop`, when B is `taken` | Bound, as in case 4. The guard on the state fails. | Settling. Written, decided `refused`, `too-late`. The entry holds no effect. The count of B is 0. |
| 6 | The wrong owner: a `stop` from P with the ticket of B | The selector gives B. The `where` fails: P is not the owner of B. | Not bound: new work. Not decided. Transport answers "retry". The count of B stays 1, and nothing of A changes. |
| 7 | A repeat: the envelope of case 4, delivered again | It was decided. | Answered from its deciding entry. The selector does not run. Nothing is drawn, and nothing is written. |
| 8 | After case 5, a second `stop` from Q for B, in another envelope | The selector gives B. Its count is 0. | Not bound: new work. Not decided. |
| 9 | No match. A `stop` from Q with a ticket for which G holds no job: its `start` has not arrived | The index returns no job. The selector gives none, and the rule `job-of` does not run. | Not bound: new work, which needs 1 entry and 1 item. Not decided. With that room it is written, decided `applied`, and the rule `open-stopped` opens the job as `gone`. That job is final and holds nothing. |
| 10 | The envelope of case 9, which was not decided, delivered again after room was free, the `start` for its ticket was recorded, and G is full again | It is no repeat. The index now returns the job, which is `queued`, of Q, with a count of 1. | Bound. Settling. Written with no free room, decided `applied`. |
| 11 | A `stop` from P for A and a `stop` from Q for B, in either order | Each lookup returns its own job, and the selector gives it. Neither is given the board, so neither reads `slot` or `judging`. | Each is bound and written. The counts of A and of B are each drawn once, in either order. C is as it was. |
| 12 | A `stop` from R for C, which `board.slot` names and which is `taken` | The selector gives C. Bound. The guard on the state fails. | Settling. Written, decided `refused`, `too-late`. A job that the board names is found by the same rule as one that it does not name. |
| 13 | After case 4, a `stop` from Q for B in another envelope: B is `gone` | The index returns B, which is final and is still indexed. The rule gives B. | Not bound: new work. Not decided. |
| 14 | The `stop` of case 4, when the rule `open-stopped` returns an `open` | An `open` effect of a rule, in a bound delivery. | A fault. Nothing is written, and the delivery is retried. |
| 15 | The `stop` of case 4, when the rule `job-of` returns the ID of A, or of the board | Neither is an item that the selector was given: it was given B only. | A fault. Nothing is written. |
| 16 | The `stop` of case 4 at a runtime, and at a verifier that starts from a checkpoint and builds the index from the items of its state | The same state and the same message. Each makes the same lookup, and gets B. | The same selection, B, and the same entry. |
| 17 | A replay of the entries of cases 4 and 5 | It builds the index by folding, makes the lookup on the state before each entry, and runs `job-of` on what the lookup returns and on the recorded message. It derives the binding, the draw and both amounts. | `consistent`. With case 5 read as new work at a full scope: `mismatch`. |
| 18 | A selector with no index: the data of M, where the mark `job-of` states `code`, `row` and `item` only | A binding selector states no `index`. | Refused by the validator, `bound-source`. |
| 19 | An index that is not declared: the data of M, where `job` states no `indexes`, or lists `owner` only | The `index` of the mark is no slot that the `indexes` of its type lists. | Refused by the validator, `bound-source`. |
| 20 | A key of the wrong type: the data of M, where the mark states `key: "note"` and `note` is a field of the type `text`; or where the field `ticket` is optional; or where it is a fact under another definition | The `key` is no required field of the handler whose type is the type of the slot. | Refused by the validator, `bound-source`, in each of the three. |
| 21 | The data of M, where `job` lists in `indexes` a slot that is not fixed, a slot of the type `text`, or five slots | Check 6. | It does not validate, `unsupported-definition`, in each of the three. |
| 22 | Two matches, of which one is final. After case 9 was written, a `start` from Q for the same ticket opens a second job, `queued`, and G is full again. A `stop` from Q with that ticket, in a new envelope | The index returns both, in order of item ID: the job of case 9, which is `gone`, and the second. The rule gives the second, which is not final. Q is its owner, and its count is 1. | Bound. Settling. Written, decided `applied`. The second job is `gone`. The job of case 9 is as it was. |
| 23 | The index at the head. While room is free a `start` from Q for a new ticket is written, and fills G. The next entry is a `stop` from Q with that ticket | The index holds the job from the transaction of its opening. The lookup returns it. | Bound. Settling. Written. At a runtime whose index holds no row for that job, no lookup is answered: the delivery is not judged, and is retried. |
| 24 | More than 8. G holds nine jobs with one ticket, which M's `start` does not refuse, and a `stop` arrives with that ticket | The index returns 9 rows, which is more than 8. | A fault. The rule does not run. Nothing is written, and the delivery is retried. It stays so: the nine keys are fixed, and no job is removed. |
| 25 | The whole reference, among many. G holds 40 more jobs of Q, each with a ticket in the same scope as the ticket of B and at another position. The `stop` of case 4 | A key is the whole fact reference. No other ticket equals it. The index returns B only, with 1 row read and 1 item. | As case 4. The work is the same as with three jobs. |

Owner: B1 for cases 1 to 3 and 18 to 21; B2 for cases 4 to 15 and 22 to
25, on real storage; B9 for cases 16 and 17. Every rule is a stand-in.
This shows that a request for an item which neither reference of the
board names is bound and decided with no free room, by an index that the
type declares, with the controls of another sender and of a repeat. It
shows that a selector with no index does not validate. It proves nothing
about a rule of a destination, and it measures no work.

### 18.54 Two marks on one item, and a state settlement beside them

New in revision 22 (section 6.4, "Several marks on one item"; section
17.2, "A marker duty"; the verdict `dc1da38a`, its second finding). M is
a made-up definition. Its item type `job` has the states `open`, `held`
and `done`, of which `done` is final, and two value slots, `a` and `b`,
each of the type `bool`, required, with `default: false`. The act
`start` opens a `job`, `open`. Each of the other acts is a transition on
a job. `mark-a` states `settles: { of: "on", sets: "a", in: ["open",
"held"] }` and one `value` effect that sets `a` to `true`. `mark-a-far`
states `settles: { of: "on", sets: "a", in: ["open"] }`, the same
effect, and one `tell` with empty clauses. `mark-b` states `settles: {
of: "on", sets: "b", in: ["open", "held"] }` and sets `b` to `true`.
`close` states `settles: { of: "on", in: ["open"] }` and sets the state
`done`. M has no timed rule. G is a scope under M with a budget of
entries. Four more definitions, M2 to M5, are named in the cases. Every
number is made up.

| Case | The input | Judged | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The data of M | The three duties of a job that is `open` with both marks `false`. (job, `a`): the larger of `mark-a`, which is 1 entry, and `mark-a-far`, which is 1 entry and the 2 of its request. (job, `b`): 1. The state duty, for `close`: 1. | It validates. The job reserves 3 and 1 and 1: 5 entries, and 1 pending request. |
| 2 | `start` at G, whose free room is 6 entries | New work: its entry and the 5 of the job. | Written. With room for 5 it is refused `scope-full`, and names entries. |
| 3 | After case 2, at G with no free room: `mark-a`, then `mark-b` | Each settles its own duty. | Both are written. After the first the job reserves 2, for `b` and for `close`, and 2 entries are released. After the second it reserves 1. |
| 4 | The other order: `mark-b`, then `mark-a` | The same. | Both are written. After the first the job reserves 4. After the second it reserves 1. |
| 5 | The control, by the sentence of revision 21: one reservation for the item, the largest of its forms, which is 3 | `mark-b`, `mark-a-far` and `close` are each a first settlement of the job. They write 1, 3 and 1 entries, with what they start. | 5 entries against a reservation of 3: used plus reserved would grow. That is the verdict's case. By case 1 the job reserves 5. |
| 6 | One mark is `true` already: after `mark-a` of case 3, a second `mark-a` | (job, `a`) is completed. The job awaits nothing for `a`. | New work. At G with no free room it is refused `scope-full`. |
| 7 | Two forms for one mark: after case 2, at G with no free room, `mark-a-far` | It settles (job, `a`), which reserved for the larger of its two forms. | Written. Its request is sent, and the request's duty holds the 2 entries. A `mark-a` after it is new work: the duty was one, and one form settled it. |
| 8 | A state settlement beside the marks: after case 2, at G with no free room, `close` | It settles the state duty. The job is `done`, outside the `in` of both marks. | Written. Both marker duties end with their slots `false`, and their 4 entries are released. The job reserves nothing. |
| 9 | M2: M where `close` sets the state `held`, and an act `finish` states `settles: { of: "on", in: ["held"] }` and sets `done` | The state duty of a job that is `open` with both marks `false`: `close`, and what the job reserves in `held`, which is `finish`, (job, `a`) by `mark-a`, and (job, `b`). | It validates. The state duty is 1 and 3: 4 entries. The job reserves 3 and 1 and 4: 8. |
| 10 | Under M2, after `mark-a` | `a` is completed, and is in no later closure. | The state duty is 1 and 2: 3 entries. The job reserves 1 and 3: 4. After `close` it reserves 2, for `finish` and for `b`. |
| 11 | M3: M with `start`, `mark-a` and `mark-b` only, where `mark-a` lists `open` and also sets the state `held`, and `mark-b` lists `held` and also sets the state `open` | The path is `a`, then `b`. In `open` again, `a` is completed. | It validates. A job that is `open` reserves 2: `mark-a`, and (job, `b`) in `held`. A count that took `a` as `false` again would not end. |
| 12 | M4: M3 where `mark-b` also sets the state `open` of a second job, which a field names | Another item of the type is left in the `in` of `mark-a`, with no mark completed. From there `mark-a` and `mark-b` follow again. | Refused by the validator, `reserve-unbounded`. |
| 13 | M5: platform data, in which a handler `flag` states `settles: { of: "also.job", sets: "a", in: ["open"] }`, no written effect, and an effect mark with `most: { effects: 2 }`, whose rule sets `a` to `true` | A rule of a form that declares `settles` returns no change of state. The mark counts none. | It validates, and (job, `a`) reserves 1 entry. A `flag` at a scope with no free room is settling, and is written. |
| 14 | Under M5, a `flag` whose rule returns a `state` effect | A change of state by a rule of a settling form. | A fault. Nothing is written. |
| 15 | A replay of the entries of cases 3 and 8 | It derives the pending duties, the marks that are `true` and both amounts at each head. | `consistent`. |

Owner: B1 for cases 1, 5, 9 and 11 to 13, at the validator; B2 for cases
2 to 4, 6 to 8, 10 and 14, on real storage; B9 for case 15. A script
made the sums of cases 1 to 5 and 8 to 11. This shows that two marks on
one item are two duties, in both orders, with one mark set, with two
forms for one mark and with a state settlement beside them. It measures
no number.
